6p40oarauhdcihhmi2s41ap4v0: A sample as a point of saturation space: atanh, written as log(2 / (1 − x) − 1) / 2 so x appears once and running it backwards is one answer (tanh).
p3689sdkb9acrs9rn1effptkjh: Overdrive: scale the sample in saturation space and come back, tanh(amount · atanh(x)). It keeps −1 to 1, is the sample itself at amount 1, and pushes towards ±1 as amount grows, a soft clipper whose way back nobody wrote.
gtggrege5fntpp0jnoqqma0750: Haar's split in lifting steps: each pair of samples as their difference (the fast band) and the second plus half of it, their average (the slow band). Each step has one unknown when run backwards, so the join is plain arithmetic. An odd sample out is no split.
i90rf905lbj53b6vquo0h0htnv: Overdrive the slow band and leave the fast one: the low strings break up, the pick attack stays clean.
dfhu269hvu9gf9l1ec2u3msrh2: The loudest sample of a block.
475dipv39at80j1pp1bvbnek24: Over the threshold, the gain takes the level three quarters of the way back to it, in log terms: 4 to 1.
doehgd5oecbm85l38kcfe09rr3: The samples, each at its gain, and the level after the last: the level is the sample, or the last level a little lower (it falls by half in about 0.06 s at 48 kHz), so it rises at once and falls slowly.
p9nk5uc3phat71cbkh74g399th: A compressor: the level follows the samples from one to the next and from block to block, in a cell, so it is the same whatever size the blocks are.
5f9f72h412r7qsnd1deq5jb2jr: The pedal: a block of samples split into bands, the slow one driven, joined again, by as much as the amount cell says when the block comes (so a knob can turn it while it plays), compressed, and brought back to the loudness that came in. With the driven cell at 0 it plays the block as it came (bypass), for comparing.
428fed412gt27dp6lp0ac3s6i6: The pedal with its drive at 32: what `lab render examples/pedal --main pedal in.wav` plays over a WAV file.
neq5v393ngu69s6qdq0qsdof9t: The pedal as a page: each button plays the pedal on an input; Clean and Driven switch the effect off and on, Softer and Harder turn its drive (from 1, the sample itself, to 256), and the picture shows what the drive does to a sine. The cells are read on the audio thread too, so they turn while the sound plays.
nnl0h7o41eq445jdudnmlvkgrv: The mean of the squares of the samples: how loud they are, the square of their RMS.
3m906neppel32odkgvaecn94n3: The loudness so far, `level` (a mean square), after one more sample: mostly what it was, a little of the new sample's square, so it follows over about 2000 samples (0.04 s at 48 kHz).
qjifb4257skiraqhdnklku1qth: The gain that brings loudness `wet` to loudness `dry`, never over 4, so the pedal can't turn a quiet input (or a microphone hearing the speakers) up and up; 1 while nothing has come.
g04jt25lmra2jaiajr08nv5ptd: Sample `y` at gain `g`, but never past 0.95 either way: the speakers stop at 1.
5tkfspbmh8urhn7qkchnlde0go: `wet`, sample by sample, at the loudness of `dry`: both loudnesses follow their samples from `dry level` and `wet level`, and each wet sample takes the gain between them. Gives the samples and the two loudnesses after the last, for the next block.
jub03hb981gnitgr0lv26vln43: `wet` at the loudness of `dry`, the loudnesses carried from block to block in two cells, so it is the same whatever size the blocks are. So the drive changes the tone, not the volume, and Clean against Driven is a fair comparison: louder always sounds better, so listening tests match levels first (prior art: level-matched A/B, as in ITU-R BS.1116).
